job.title: Head of Assurance | Remediation Program
job.description:
The Role

Ink Recruitment has been engaged to recruit a Head of Assurance for a well-renowned, Sydney-based financial services organisation. Reporting to a member of the executive team and sitting on the program leadership team, you will provide independent second-line oversight across a critical remediation program, with accountability for assurance over remediation design, delivery, reconciliation, financial integrity and closure.

You will lead one direct report with support from a broader project team. This is a role for someone who brings independent judgement and constructive challenge, testing whether methodologies, controls and customer outcomes are working as intended and backed by complete, regulator-ready evidence, while keeping clear separation from the design and execution teams.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead independent assurance across solution design, operational delivery and program closure, with a risk-based assurance plan aligned to remediation priorities, material risks and regulatory expectations
  • Assess design and delivery of methodologies, treatment plans, population logic, calculations, processes and controls, and test that remediation is applied consistently across customer, claims, premium and payment outcomes
  • Oversee end-to-end reconciliation across populations, customer outcomes, claims, refunds, payments and financial records, ensuring exceptions and variances are investigated, resolved and evidenced
  • Evaluate control effectiveness across remediation processes and hand-offs, maintaining transparent findings and actions and confirming root causes are sustainably addressed
  • Define closure requirements and provide an independent view on whether outcomes, reconciliation, control actions and residual risk support workstream and program closure
  • Report with clarity to executive, Steering Committee, Board and Board committees, and support regulatory engagement with complete, consistent and defensible evidence
  • Lead and coordinate, managing your direct report and working with specialist support across Risk, Finance, Legal, Internal Audit and external advisers

Desired Experience

  • Banking or financial services background with strong audit or assurance experience
  • Working knowledge of remediation programs, ideally large-scale regulatory remediation
  • Proven track record designing and leading risk-based assurance across complex programs or operational processes
  • Strong reconciliation and financial integrity capability, including investigating and resolving exceptions and variances
  • Experience assessing control design and operating effectiveness and validating sustainable closure of findings
  • Confident Board, executive, audit and regulatory reporting, with clear and authoritative advice
  • Sharp analytical judgement, professional scepticism and the confidence to challenge senior stakeholders constructively
  • Tertiary qualification in risk, audit, finance, accounting, law, business or a related field, or equivalent senior experience
  • Availability to start ASAP

Benefits

  • High-visibility role with direct exposure to the Board and executive
  • Genuine independence and the mandate to shape assurance practice
  • Opportunity to embed lasting reconciliation, evidence and closure discipline across the organisation
  • Incredibly collaborative culture with supportive executives setting the right tone from the top
  • Up to $245,000 package. Remote or hybrid working available

How to Apply

If you bring independent judgement, rigour and a commitment to fair customer outcomes, we’d love to hear from you. Submit your CV to hello@inkrecruitment.com.au or apply via Seek below.

For a confidential chat, contact Jen Jones at Ink Recruitment on +61 (0)409 926 897.

job.title: Senior Analyst - Compliance
job.description:

About you

  • 5+ years in a compliance, risk or regulatory role

  • Hybrid working, 3 days a week in the Brisbane office
  • Broad exposure across marketing compliance, licensing and control room work
  • A growing team within a respected global investment business

job.title: Head of Governance and People & Culture
job.description:
The Role

We’re recruiting a Head of Governance, People & Culture for a well-established not-for-profit that delivers aged care, NDIS, veterans’ and clinical services across Tasmania. After a period of transformation, the organisation has a new leadership team, two years of stability behind it and a clear plan for growth.

Reporting to the COO, this role leans primarily into governance, risk and compliance, with strategic oversight of people and culture. You’ll start by driving the continuous improvement plan, then build a sustainable clinical and corporate governance framework and help operationalise a new purpose-built 24/7 respite centre.

The role starts with no direct reports, but there is strong potential to build a team quickly as the function grows.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop, embed and maintain an enterprise governance, risk and compliance framework with clear accountabilities, registers, controls, reporting and escalation pathways
  • Drive the continuous improvement plan and oversee the policy framework, internal assurance calendar, audit coordination and corrective actions
  • Partner with clinical and service leaders to build sustainable clinical governance, quality and safeguarding systems aligned with aged care, NDIS and other contracted-service standards
  • Coordinate enterprise risk assessment across workforce, WHS, operational, clinical interface, privacy, financial control and regulatory risks
  • Provide clear governance advice and high-quality reporting to the CEO, Board and committees on emerging risks, incidents, trends and progress
  • Mature an integrated People & Culture strategy that supports the organisation’s growth and employer-of-choice commitments, working alongside existing P&C specialists
  • Oversee employee relations, investigations and employment policy, ensuring procedural fairness and alignment with industrial instruments and WHS obligations
  • Strengthen cultural and psychological safety, wellbeing and engagement across a passionate, values-driven workforce
  • Build constructive relationships with regulators, funding bodies, auditors, legal advisers and sector partners
  • Contribute to executive planning, organisational design and sustainable growth decisions as a key member of the leadership group

Skills & Experience

  • Substantial senior leadership experience in governance, risk and compliance, and/or People and Culture with a demonstrated ability to integrate these functions
  • Proven ability to develop enterprise frameworks, turn strategy into practical implementation and report confidently to executives and boards
  • Sound knowledge of Australian employment relations, workplace investigations, organisational change and procedural fairness
  • Exposure to aged care, NDIS or clinical governance standards will be well regarded.
  • A firm, steady presence balanced with genuine empathy, comfortable supporting a passionate and emotionally invested workforce while holding the line when it matters
  • Excellent judgement, discretion and stakeholder management, with the ability to juggle competing priorities
  • Experience leading and developing teams and using data to improve organisational outcomes

Benefits

  • Well remunerated role in line with the Tasmania market, with real scope to grow your role and team
  • Genuine flexibility with a monthly RDO or a fortnightly short day through compressed hours, plus 1 to 2 days working from home each week
  • Recently recognised as an Employer of Choice
  • Pet-friendly workplace with a team pet roster and a resident office dog
  • A close-knit, collaborative leadership team where everyone knows everyone
  • Purpose-driven work that makes a real difference to the Tasmanian community, NDIS participants, veterans and their families
  • Tasmanian lifestyle in Launceston, with an easy commute from every direction

A rare chance to put your stamp on governance and culture at a values-driven organisation entering an exciting growth phase.

Please submit your CV and a cover letter to hello@inkrecruitment.com.au outlining your relevant experience and motivation for this role, or apply via Seek. Or for a confidential chat, contact Jen Jones at Ink Recruitment on +61 (0)409 926 897
